title: feat(studio): the field inspector, field designer and object settings write Field change values (#36290 part 1)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9NRmimMwnUgR1DbqgHtBWM3)_

Part of #36290

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 管理员在 Studio 的字段设置和字段设计器里，原来的「记录历史」开关换成「字段修改值」三选一（默认 / 开 / 关），对象设置的「功能开关」里新增「字段修改值」；普通用户无感。
- 属于记录页「字段修改前后值」专题，落实「默认显示、对象或单个字段可关」的裁决：以前 Studio 写的是不再起作用的旧开关，管理员在界面上关不掉前后值。
- 若出错，管理员可能看到「默认」标成开而动态里实际不显示前后值（或相反），或关掉后回不到默认；改动只在设置界面，可直接撤回。
- 要你做的：无。

## What changes

Card #36290 part ① (PR 3 of 4; ruling 7076513167 point 1: "Old → new is shown by default on every object's record page; an object, or a single field, can turn it off."). PR 1 (#36399) gave the runtime `fieldHistory` (field) and `enable.fieldHistory` (object); #36580 gave the metadata form a three-way `field-history` widget. The Studio's own producers still wrote the old key. This PR moves all three named in the release comment.

**Field inspector** (`ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`, Advanced section)
- The "Track history" box (`value={!!def.trackHistory}`, `patchDef({ trackHistory: v || undefined })`) is gone. Measured reason: since PR 1 a field's `trackHistory: false` reads like absent and `true` does only what `fieldHistory: true` does for a media or JSON type (spec describe of `FieldSchema.trackHistory`), so a second box beside Field change values could only mislead. A stored `trackHistory` is never written or removed here; it is still read, because `resolveFieldHistory` reads it.
- New row "Field change values": Default / On / Off over the field's `fieldHistory`. Default removes the key (`unsetDefKey`, not a patch to `undefined`); On / Off write `true` / `false`.
- Default names what it resolves to through `resolveFieldHistory` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the predicate the activity writer uses. Unlike the form widget, this rail holds the object document, so it passes the object: an object with `enable.fieldHistory: false` makes every field's Default read "Default (Off)", and a note under the row says the object's off wins.
- The row sits inside the existing `DisplayPatchLock`, so on a read-only base field it is locked with the same reason as its neighbours (`fieldHistory` is not on `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`).

**Object settings** (`ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`, Features card)
- New row "Field change values" (`enable.fieldHistory`), next to "Field change history" (`enable.trackHistory`). Ticked unless the stored value is a literal `false`. Unticking writes `false`; ticking again REMOVES the key (unset already means on, so no `true` the author did not need). Sibling `enable` keys are kept, as for every other row.
- The Field change history description no longer says "pair with per-field history tracking to pick which field diffs are summarized" (no longer true); it points to Field change values.

**Field designer** (`plugin-designer` `FieldDesigner.tsx`, the drawer behind `MetadataFieldsPage` and the `field-designer` SDUI type)
- The Advanced section's Track History switch wrote `trackHistory: data.trackHistory === true` on every save, create and edit. It is replaced by Field Change Values with the same three choices. The update path no longer names `trackHistory`: a stored value rides the `...editingField` spread, and a created field carries neither key at Default.
- Default's label depends on the type, which the author can change in the same drawer, and a drawer select's options are static. So the choice is drawn as two rows under form-local names, one per resolved default, each shown by a `visibleWhen` built from `resolveFieldHistory` over `DESIGNER_FIELD_TYPES` (with the field's stored `trackHistory`). The save reads the row shown for the saved type, which is the one on screen at the click. Neither form-local name reaches the model.
- `DesignerFieldDefinition` (`@object-ui/types`) and its zod mirror gain an optional `fieldHistory`. Both save paths carry it: `MetadataFieldsPage` (`toDesignerField` / `fromDesignerField`) and `MetadataService.toFieldPayload`. Default writes `fieldHistory: undefined`, which overrides the carried value and is dropped on the wire, so a stored key is removed. That is the converters' existing clear-by-absence rule.
- It cannot import `fieldHistoryChoice.ts`, because app-shell depends on plugin-designer. What it shares is the rule (`resolveFieldHistory` from `@objectstack/spec/data`). Its own copy of the choice-to-value mapping is two lines. Its strings are the language-pack keys `appDesigner.fieldDesigner.fieldHistory`, `fieldHistoryDefault`, `fieldHistoryOn` and `fieldHistoryOff`, in all 11 locales and the designer's defaults table. They replace `appDesigner.fieldDesigner.trackHistory`.

**Shared logic** (`metadata-admin/fieldHistoryChoice.ts`, new): the three choices, the value each writes and their wording, used by both the inspector row and the #36580 `field-history` widget (refactored onto it; its behaviour and its 10 pins unchanged). The controls stay separate on purpose: the widget is a `WidgetProps` renderer that sees one form row and no object; the inspector row is an `InspectorSelectField` with the inspector's label and lock semantics and the whole object in hand.

**Strings** (studio namespace, en + zh; the other locales fall back to en by that namespace's design): `designer.field.fieldHistory`, `designer.field.fieldHistoryObjectOff`, `engine.studio.settings.capFieldHistory`, `engine.studio.settings.capFieldHistoryDesc`; `engine.studio.settings.capTrackHistoryDesc` reworded; `designer.field.trackHistory` removed with its box.

Not in this PR: record-page rows (part ②, landed as #36613), the per-field history card (part ③).

## Tests

- New `ObjectFieldInspector.fieldHistory-36290.test.tsx` (7): Default (On) for a one-line type; Default (Off) for image / json / password and Default (On) once `trackHistory: true`; Off writes `false`, On writes `true`; Default after Off removes the key; no Track history box, no `trackHistory` written, a stored one kept; the object's off makes Default (Off) and shows the note; control: no note otherwise.
- New describe in `ObjectSettingsPanel.test.tsx` (4): checked for unset and `true`, unchecked only for `false`; untick writes `false` with siblings kept; re-tick removes the key with siblings kept; labelled by its own title.
- New `FieldDesigner.fieldHistory-36290.test.tsx` (9), on the real `FieldDesigner` with a drawer double that captures its schema and calls its own `onSuccess`. The cases: two rows and no Track History row, with the labels; for every designer type exactly one row's `visibleWhen` evaluates true (through `evalFieldPredicate`, the form's own evaluator), and it is the one `resolveFieldHistory` names; a stored `trackHistory: true` moves a media type to the Default (On) row; an untouched edit writes neither key; Off writes `false`, On on a media type writes `true`; a stored `false` opens as Off and Default removes it; a stored `trackHistory` is kept; a type changed in the drawer saves what is on screen; a created field at Default carries neither key.
- New `MetadataFieldsPage.fieldHistory-36290.test.tsx` (4), on PUT bytes through the real page and a real `MetadataClient`. A stored `fieldHistory: false` survives and no `trackHistory` is written; a stored `trackHistory: true` survives and gains no `fieldHistory`; a field with neither key gains neither; every PUT field parses through `FieldSchema`.
- Extended: `MetadataService.fieldKeyCarryOver.test.ts` adds `fieldHistory` to its populated entry and its clearable keys; `designer-zod-arms-10859.test.ts` adds `fieldHistory` to the fully populated `field-designer` document.
- Forced test changes: `ObjectFieldInspector.displayPatchReason-28986.test.tsx` names the Field change values combobox instead of the removed Track history checkbox among the locked controls; `ObjectSettingsPanel.businessWording-36512.test.tsx` lists `enable.fieldHistory` among the keys the tab writes. `ObjectFieldInspector.externalIdNotOffered-26674.test.tsx` and `ObjectFieldInspector.retiredIndexed.test.tsx` listed Track history among the Advanced siblings that still render; they name Field change values, and (being edited) now pay the formula and lint loads at module top, as `check:test-source-alias` requires. `FieldDesigner.externalIdNotOffered-26674.test.tsx` and `MetadataFieldsPage.externalIdRoundTrip-26674.test.tsx` used the Track History row as their positive control; they now use the Field Change Values row.


## Acceptance notes

- The field designer's Default label follows the drawer's type and the object is not in hand, so an object with `enable.fieldHistory: false` is not reflected there, the same accepted bound as #36580's widget. Neither `FieldDesigner` nor `MetadataFieldsPage` is mounted by the Console today; both are published exports, and `field-designer` is a registered SDUI type.
- A stored field `trackHistory: true` on a media or JSON type makes Default read "Default (On)"; such a field can still be turned off with Off, but not returned to the type's off-by-default without editing the key in the form. That is the resolver's answer, not a UI choice.
- `ui/AGENTS.md` #2 (package README and `content/docs/frontend/` page) not edited: outside this part's file surface.
- Screenshots NOT MEASURED (no Console build or backend run here).

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `ui/packages/plugin-designer/src/FieldDesigner.tsx`: the `fieldHistoryRows` memo (two rows, `visibleWhen` built from `resolveFieldHistory`) and `fieldHistoryFromForm`, which picks the row for the SAVED type on both save paths.
2. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectSettingsPanel.tsx`: `patchEnable` with `unsetWhenOn` (re-ticking removes `enable.fieldHistory`, keeps siblings).
3. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`: the Field change values row and the object-off note inside `DisplayPatchLock`.

Two-minute check: open Studio, an object, Settings, Features: "Field change values" is ticked. Untick, save, and reopen the object JSON: it shows `enable.fieldHistory: false`. Tick again: the key is gone. Then open a field's Advanced section: "Field change values" reads "Default (Off)" with the note under it.
